title: Day 4 - Babies I, J, K, L, M & N
section: Lucy Letby - Examination-in-chief by Ben Myers LC

blocks.text: Lucy Letby - Examination-in-chief day 4: Babies I, J, K, L, M & N
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)
Tuesday, 16 May 2023
(In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)

Good morning, Ms Letby. I'm going to ask if you could make sure you keep your voice up as loudly as you can when you give evidence today. I'll remind you from time to time. It's just important that the people taking a note on the other end of the microphones can hear what you say clearly. So just remember to keep your voice up, as if you're addressing the back row of the jury. No one will complain if your voice is loud.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yesterday when we concluded we had been dealing with the final event involving [Baby I], count 12 on our indictment. That's the event on the night of the 22nd to 23 October. We'd looked at how that was in two parts: what happened a couple of minutes to midnight on the 22nd when she was with Ashleigh Hudson and then what happened at about 01.06 in the morning. And I had been asking you about your involvement at that point.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So with apologies for going back perhaps a couple of sentences, could I ask you, were you involved in the measures that were given to support [Baby I] after the second part of that collapse, after 01.06?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you recall, as you sit there now, when it was that you had first been in the nursery dealing with her, whether it's from earlier in the event or later on? I'm not prejudging it, but can you help us with when it was?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I couldn't say.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you recall whether you were already in the nursery when she deteriorated that second time or if you came to the nursery after she had deteriorated? Do you recall that now?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But you do recall being there at some point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I recall going to her at some point and she was crying and I helped Ashleigh settle her, but I can't remember on which occasion that was.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. And did you take a part in what happened afterwards with the attempts to support [Baby I] and help her?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you there when, sadly, [Baby I] died?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were the parents there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you involved in helping the bereaved family after [Baby I] had died?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it was Ashleigh's first experience of a death, so I assisted her with the bereavement paperwork and process.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Did she play a part in it as well or was that handed across to you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, Ashleigh remained the designated nurse for [Baby I], but I just supported her with the things that needed to be done.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If she had been more experienced in a situation like this, would there have been the same need for you to give support in the way that you did?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I gave her more support because it was her first time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we put up tile 297 from the fourth [Baby I] sequence, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: [Baby I]'s funeral was on 10 November 2015, 12 o'clock. Were you aware as to whether or not members of staff went to that funeral?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, members of staff did go.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you know how many did go?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Um... I know it was more than two, I couldn't say for definite, but a few nurses went.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was it a common event for nurses to attend a funeral if a baby had died?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No. Usually it's if the parents request somebody to be there, then the unit would represent them.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you able to go to the funeral?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I was working.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we put up the shift pattern, please, at page 33225? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we just enlarge the dates for November, the lower part of this. The funeral was on the 10th, as we've seen. Had you been working the night before the funeral?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you'd have finished at some time on that morning?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, and I was due in again that night as well.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. So you weren't able to go?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you convey your sympathies to the family in any other way since you couldn't go to the funeral?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. I was advised by other staff that I could send a card to the family via the people that were going to the funeral and that's what I did.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we put up the images that we've got of a card at exhibit 13163, please, Mr Murphy. 13163 and 13164.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's 13163. Then could we look at 13164? We have seen these before.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: First of all, Ms Letby, what is the item that we're looking at on those pictures?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: This is the sympathy card that I wrote for [Baby I]'s family.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And did you send it to them?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I gave it to one of the nurses that was attending the funeral for them to pass on.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We know, again, from our agreed facts, it's agreed facts 41 and 42, that images of that card were recovered from the handset of your phone and they show that the images were taken at 7.34, so a little after 4.30 (sic) in the morning, of 10 November 2015. And again, as with the other images we've looked at, the coordinates there were of a location in the south-west corner of the Women's and Children's building at the hospital?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So, first of all, about 7.30 on 10 November, where would you have been?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: At work.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that where you took the photograph?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then you handed it to a member of staff to take to the funeral?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. I'm not sure who I handed it to, but yes, it was given to one of the staff members going.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was it unusual for you to take a photograph of a card?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No. I photograph the majority of cards that I send or letters. That's just normal behaviour for me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we have a look, please, Mr Murphy, at an item you have designated D29. It's from the exhibits in this case, pages 33733, 33734 and 33735. We're going to go through these images and ask you about them, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: This is from the exhibits we've been served.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Page J33732. Just look at the pages. Could we look at the next page, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's actually the end of the exhibit we just looked at in fact for the [Family of Babies E & F]. This is the page I wanted to go to. This is page 1. Is it possible to rotate that? We can see names there and we have to have them so we know who this is related to. That's the first page of this. Who is this card from?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's me writing the card to somebody.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right then. What's the card for?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's congratulating my close friend on the birth of her daughter.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is this to do with work or to do with friends?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, this is a friend. Nothing to do with work.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we look at the next page, please. Just enlarge that, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Is that another picture of the card?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The same?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we look at the next page, please, Mr Murphy?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Page 33735 from the exhibits. If it's not there, don't worry. We see in fact that image follows on in the exhibits from the image of the card to the [Family of Babies E & F]; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, the [Family of Baby I], I apologise.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: This is the same card on the two photographs that we're looking at?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it unusual for you to take a picture of a card that you are sending?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, that's regularly what I do.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And when you say regularly, is that something to do with work or for other reasons?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, for anything that I'm sending or receiving, I usually take a copy of that, and that's something I've done for many years.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, can I just be clear? The two images we have seen are both of the same card but they were two images that were taken? And there is a third one that we haven't seen?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, I'll check that, my Lord. It's how it comes from the exhibit so it's included in this way. We've got page 33 and then 34. They appear to be in fact the same image, whether it's the same photograph or a --
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I think there's only one. I think this is the photograph and the other one is zoomed in.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So it's just one photograph?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It's one photograph but zoomed in.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That's what I just wanted to clarify because it wasn't clear, if we can. All right. Anyway, it's the same card, whatever it is. Whether it's one or two images, it's the same card and it's to a family friend congratulating them on the birth of their child.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you. And you say that's something you do, cards that are sent or cards that are received?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: One of those things you do, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. I'm going to move from the case relating to [Baby I] and we'll turn to count 13 on this indictment, which is the case relating to [Baby J]. So we can put aside anything we have for [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: First of all, as we've been doing, we'll just remind ourselves of the basic facts relating to this particular count, count 13. I'm going to ask Mr Murphy if we could start by going to tile 1 on the [Baby J] sequence and just go into that, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We can see, Ms Letby, the details of birth, [Baby J] was born on 31 October 2015 at 15.00 hours, a gestation of 32 weeks and 2 days, weight, 1.709 kilograms, born by caesarean.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Could we go into the tile, please? If we scroll down a little bit, please. Thanks very much.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Looking at the detail, there are various problems in pregnancy for [Baby J]. Sadly, we can see that a twin died in utero. There was twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome for [Baby J]; that's where
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: identical twins share a placenta, we've heard that, and there can be uneven blood flow.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There had been, we were told in evidence, antenatal, so before birth, rupture of the membranes, and just to assist everybody with their recollection, it's [Baby J], ladies and gentlemen, where, after birth, and after some production of bile, an abdominal X-ray revealed a problem with the bowel loops and [Baby J] went to Alder Hey Children's Hospital for an ileostomy, which she had on 1 November. That's detail that can help place where we are on the indictment.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: As a result of that ileostomy, she was provided with two stomas so that faeces could be recycled outside the body and there was a Broviac line inserted as well.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Does that assist you with what we're dealing with as well, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby J] returned to the Countess of Chester Hospital on 10 November 2015. Count 13 that we are dealing with relates to events on 27 November 2015, so a couple of weeks later or thereabouts.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Now, with the assistance of the neonatal review I'm going to remind you and the rest of us, Ms Letby, if it's needed, of the events we're looking at because there's almost two pairs of events that we're dealing with on 27 November. The easiest way to remind ourselves of this is to go to the neonatal review. So I recommend actually getting the paper copy if you would, ladies and gentlemen, and you do that too, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I've got it.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll be grateful to Mr Murphy for putting it up on the screen.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we open up this neonatal review, Ms Letby, could you go to page 4, please? Ladies and gentlemen, if you could go to -- it should say page 4 of 8. At this point the purpose of this is just to remind ourselves of what we're dealing with and when.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I have suggested it's helpful to think of this in the way of two pairs of events, but think of it as you wish, of course.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we look at page 4 of 11 and enlarge the section which goes from, let's say, line 75 to line 90, the first pair, as they're recorded, are at lines 77 and 87.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We can see at line 77 at 4.40, as it's recorded here, in the care of Nicola Dennison, who was the nurse designated to [Baby J], it's recorded on the apnoea/brady/fit chart and we'll have a look at the detail of that. There's an event at 04.40 and then, if we look down to line 87, again with Nicola Dennison, there's an event at 05.03 recorded on the apnoea/brady/fit chart and we'll see that. so there's a pair of events there, 4.40 and 5.03.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Both events relating to desaturations to 30% and then 50%, although in the evidence there was a question raised as to whether the percentages were the other way round. But in any event, there are desaturations on two occasions, 4.40 and 5.03. Nicola Dennison was the nurse caring.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Then if we go over the page to page 5 of 8, we actually come to those that have been identified for the purposes of the charge on the indictment, and they're easier to pick out because they've got the black bars across them. I'm going to ask if we can enlarge the section from lines 131 to 150 so we can place them.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: This second pair, one is at line 134 at 6.56, simply down as "[Baby J] event", and then at line 148 at 7.24, another event relating to [Baby J]. Again, these events relate to low desaturations and associated with clenching of hands and stiff limbs and a description given by Dr Gibbs, "Eyes deviated to the left", and the period that they lasted.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So just to help us keep in mind, it's one count but we looked at a number of different events. The first pair there for Nicola Dennison, 4.40 and 5.03. And then the two which you've got in front of you now, Ms Letby, members of the jury, on page 5, 6.56 and 7.24.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We can take the neonatal review down, though we will be going back to it, so if we keep this out for the time being, ladies and gentlemen. You too, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Let me ask you some general questions first about [Baby J]. How familiar were you with stomas when [Baby J] first came on to the unit, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'd had very little experience with stomas. I'd seen a couple at Liverpool Women's on my training there but otherwise I had no experience.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And are you able to say how others that you worked alongside were in terms of familiarity with stomas?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Very similar. So a lot of the staff had no direct relevant sort of recent experience with stoma care.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby J] had had the procedure, the ileostomy, at the Alder Hey Children's Hospital.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What is it that children or babies go to Alder Hey for principally?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: For surgery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. So is that sort of surgery something that would routinely be done at the Countess of Chester?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, that's not something that can be done at the Countess of Chester, it's something they have to go to a tertiary centre for.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Therefore do you regularly find yourself looking after babies who have had surgery like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How familiar, from what you could see, did nurses appear to be in handling the stoma bags and recycling?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I don't recall anybody being overly confident in doing it because it had been a long time for anybody -- for anybody to have had any recent experience of the stoma.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you able to say who was involved, a lot of the time, in dealing with the bags and the recycling?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Predominantly it was the parents, we took their lead, very much so.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And why was it that the parents knew what to do from what you could tell?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: They had been taught how to do it in Alder Hey and they were very attentive to [Baby J], so they knew what to do far better than we did at the Countess.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we look at some messages relating to this and can we go first, please, Mr Murphy, to tile 45.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We're going to look at a series of messages from here through to tile 58. This is on 18 November that we start at 17.32, so it's
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: about 9 days before the events we're looking at on the indictment, but let's have a look at these.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So from [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Was just a lot going on this morning with B's discharge and liaising with stoma nurses, et cetera, plus dealing with safeguarding lol. All go. Oh, and Kate Bissell has raised about Jenny having [Baby J] has looked like she's been doing the refeeding."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to move on a little bit and then ask you some questions about this. Could we go to tile 46, please. This is 18.09, you to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Ah, keeping you busy. Has B gone? That's good. Glad Kate has done that. Was talking about it with Minna and didn't don't think it's right."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just pausing there, what are you and [Nurse E] talking about with regard to what you didn't think was right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We are there talking about the fact that Jennifer Jones- Key, who was a nursery nurse, was looking after [Baby J] and carrying out her recycling, which is dealing with the stoma bags.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What duties do nursery nurses have in the unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So generally, the nursery nurses tend to care for special care babies and predominantly do bottle feeds, breastfeeding, things like that. They don't tend to do clinical care.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there a particular band that nursery nurses are at?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: They're a band 4.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can they do intensive care?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, they can't. Nor high dependency.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Not high dependency, not intensive care?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So far as you understand, should they be involved in handling and recycling stoma bags if that is required?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, and particularly as nursing staff there were unfamiliar, nursery nurses would have been even more so unfamiliar than nursing staff.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there any reason why you had a band 4 dealing with something that presented the problems that stoma bags did?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I think the unit was very busy and we had to use staff where we could.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we go to tile 47, please. From [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yeah, you discharged her. No, I know."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Is she talking about baby B at that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Tile 48, please. You to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Glad B gone. Does Jenny not have [Baby J] tonight?"
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 49, 8 o'clock in the evening, [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "No lol."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 50, please, 20.01, from you to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Did Kate speak to Eirian then as Yvonne G approved? Bet you're pooped."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 51, 20.16, from [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yvonne G approved it? Didn't realise that as Kate spoke to Yvonne [and] Eirian on the phone when they were together today at study day."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Pause there for a moment. When it refers to "together today at study day", what's a study day?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: A study day is anything that takes place outside of the unit that's paper-based, so it might be an exam or it could just be attending lectures somewhere. So you're not on the unit yourself, you are studying something elsewhere.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you ever go on study days?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, many.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Would you ever be given material when you went on a study day?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what would you do with the material you were given?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I myself would keep it to go through it --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it unusual for you to keep -- sorry, you were saying something.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I would keep it and often refer back to it.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it unusual for you to hang on to material like that when you're given it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we move please to tile 52. 20.17:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yeah, Belinda didn't think it was right but was struggling [this is you to [Nurse E]] with allocation as only three trained, so asked Yvonne G (who was in office) and she said okay to have [Baby J] and TPN babies as would be supervised. Just off to salsa."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: 53, please. 20.18, [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "That's interesting as don't think she said that to Eirian."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: 54, next tile, you to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I bet she has got wind of Eirian not thinking it's [right] and now backtracking."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can we look at 55, please, and just go through to 58 now. [Nurse E] to you:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Apparently Eirian said she would have been okay Jenny having [Baby J], but others would need to do recycling, et cetera, but she was the one performing it."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 56:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Okay, that makes sense [you say to [Nurse E]] but Jenny was actually doing it. Hmm, don't know when to stop, do they?"
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 57 from [Nurse E] to you, 17.19 on the 19th we are now, I should say:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Nope, Laura and [Nurse B] thought it was terrible."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Then this at tile 58, 17.21 you to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "It's shocking really that they are willing to take the responsibility for things that they have no training or experience, et cetera, on. Don't think they appreciate the potential difficulties."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Pausing there, Ms Letby, should nurses take on tasks for which they have no training or experience in the care of babies like this?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When you say, "Don't think they appreciate the potential difficulties", what are you referring to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That it's a safety implication, so if they don't have the training and experience to know what they are looking for when they're dealing with stomas, assessing what the sites look like, attaching bags, then it's potentially dangerous.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And why was the unit using a nurse like that for a situation like this?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was so busy at the time, I think they were just trying to use staff wherever they could.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we look at tile 61, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just before we leave that, can I just ask this:
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "It's shocking really that they are willing to take responsibility for things that they have no training or experience, et cetera, on."
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Who is the "they"?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The nursery nurses, the band 4s.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you're saying it's shocking that the band 4s are prepared to do this?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Who's asking the band 4s to do that?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: It would be the shift leader who's allocated them.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And who were the shift leaders that would do that, whichever shift leader was allocated?
blocks.speaker: MYERS
